text: Five lessons in, and you've already touched more of Power BI than you might realize. Let's zoom all the way out and name the pattern underneath everything you've done — because it's the same pattern for the rest of this course.

Here it is: Get, Transform, Model, Visualize, Publish. Five words, and every single thing you will ever do in Power BI is one of them. Not most things — everything. Let's walk through each one, and I'll tell you exactly which chapter of this course picks it up.

Step one, Get. You connect to wherever your data lives. You did this in the last lesson with an Excel file. Chapter 2 opens this up fully — CSV files, SQL databases, web pages, REST APIs, and the choice between importing data or querying it live.

Step two, Transform. Real data is rarely clean on arrival. Power Query Editor is where you fix data types, remove what you don't need, split and combine columns — and every step you take gets recorded, so it replays automatically the next time your data refreshes. Chapter 3 is entirely this.

Step three, Model. Once your data is clean, you tell Power BI how your tables relate to each other — this is the exact screen from Lesson 3's interface tour. Chapter 4 covers the star schema and relationships properly; Chapters 5 and 6 build DAX formulas and time intelligence on top of that same model.

Step four, Visualize. This is where data turns into something a person can actually read — you built your first one last lesson. Chapter 7 covers the full range of visuals and formatting; Chapter 8 goes further, into designing a whole dashboard that reads clearly at a glance.

And step five, Publish. One button turns your file into something your team can open and share. Chapter 9 covers the Power BI service itself — workspaces, sharing, and Fabric. Chapters 10 and 11 round it out: keeping data refreshed on a schedule, and controlling exactly who can see which rows.
Get, Transform, Model, Visualize, Publish. That's the whole course, in five words, and Chapter 1 is done. Next up, Chapter 2: every way to get data into Power BI. See you there.
